elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer shall own all deliverables and work product created for Customer under this Agreement or any Exhibit"

elements.element: Vendor assigns deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: "Kubient hereby assigns the same to Customer"
"Kubient owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Auction Platform and its pre-existing technology, tools and know-how"

elements.element: Licence covers any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "to the extent any Kubient pre-existing intellectual property is embedded in such deliverables" — limited to pre-existing IP, not any Vendor IP embedded

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to ... all other data provided by, or collected on behalf of, Customer"
"Nothing in this Agreement creates any joint ownership of intellectual property"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence
Licence permits use, modification and sublicensing of deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: "to use, modify and sublicense such intellectual property as part of those deliverables" plus outright ownership of the deliverables themselves

offending_extra_words: and the subsequent Section shall be renumbered accordingly
reasons: Preferred level is incomplete: the embedded-IP licence is confined to Kubient's "pre-existing intellectual property", whereas the position requires a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.

Minimality fails: the insertion imports fallback-only rights ("worldwide", "use, modify and sublicense") into a preferred-level proposal, and adds unnecessary boilerplate ("the subsequent Section shall be renumbered accordingly") in operative text.

The clause nonetheless satisfies the fallback on its material terms (Vendor keeps generic tools/know-how; Customer gets a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence, indeed outright ownership), so it is acceptable but should be tightened to "any Kubient intellectual property embedded in the deliverables" and stripped of the fallback-only licence scope.

No assignment of Customer Data or Customer IP to Vendor is created; Vendor's data right is limited to providing the Services during the Term, and unrelated sections (compliance, disclaimer, trademarks/press release) remain untouched and effective.
